rows.grounds: present passive participle of root chid, describing one undergoing cutting
optative passive form of root chid expressing potential or counterfactual result
compound of tad and gata, indicating one who has reached that state
possessive compound of tad and manas, indicating one whose mind is absorbed in that

items.question: Does physical cutting affect one whose mind is fully absorbed in that state?
premises: A person may be physically subjected to cutting.
A person can be gone to that state with mind fixed on that.
Absorption of mind in that state alters the experience of bodily harm.
items.inference: One who has reached that state and whose mind is fixed on it is not truly cut even while being cut.
uncertainties: The referent of 'that' (tad) depends on the preceding context.
It is unclear whether the immunity described is literal or experiential.
items.plain_english: Just as one who has reached that state and whose mind is fixed on it, though being cut, is not cut.
